newsitem.title: UK: TABLE TENNIS-FORMER WORLD CHAMPION WITHDRAWS FROM CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-FORMER WORLD CHAMPION WITHDRAWS FROM CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Former champion Chire Koyama, the one time Chinese star who delights in beating her old team mates now that she plays for Japan, was forced to withdraw from the opening round of the women's singles at the world table tennis championships on Friday.
Koyama, seeded joint fifth, was scheduled to meet Latvian Olga Kartuzova, but had to pull out with a respiratory complaint.
"She has not been well for nearly a month. She has been coughing and also has some back trouble," a Japanese official said.
Koyama, the current Asian champion, was formerly known as He Zhili when she played on China's world championship winning team in 1985 and captured the individual crown two years later.

Despite not being fully fit, she won all her seven matches in the team competition here, in which Japan finished sixth, and was considered one of the few legitimate challengers to China's grip on the women's title.
China has already retained both team trophies in their chase to repeat their 1995 clean sweep of all seven golds.
The singles got underway on Friday with two rounds scheduled for both men and women, reducing the field to the last 16.
Kong Linghui opened the defence of his men's title in convincing fashion against the left-handed Dutchman Jorg de Cock, who is 278th in the world rankings, 277 places below the champion.

It was a match of staccato rallies with both players invariably going for the third-ball kill. Kong coasted home 21-13 21-9 21-18 and the only time he had to dig deeper into his impressive repertoire of strokes was when he trailed 7-12 in the third game. The 21-year-old simply raised the tempo and de Cock succumbed.
Second-seeded Swede Jan-Ove Waldner, champion in 1989 and twice runner-up, was scheduled to play later on Friday.
